summary_notes: Prospect: national TMS vendor with latency-sensitive chat support and reranking pipeline. Primary ask: predictable throughput for peak loads (holiday/logistics peaks) and contractual p95 latency guarantees. Very cost-aware but willing to commit for predictability. Prefers private VPC deployment with customer KMS. Wants explicit fallback and routing policy in SLA. Quotes: "we can't have multimillion-dollar SLA surprises during Black Friday window". SE concern: mixed workload (short chat requests + long-document rerank) will need separate pooling or autoscaling guards.
technical_requirements: Baseline steady-state QPS: 180 QPS for chat (avg request ~90 tokens), peak burst QPS: 900 for 45 minute peaks
Embeddings/rerank throughput: 350 queries/sec steady with batched encodings; token/sec estimate 1.2M tokens/day
Latency targets: chat p50 <30ms, p95 <150ms for short-turn requests; rerank p95 <350ms
Model preferences: open LLM family (quantized 4-bit variants acceptable), ability to route between full-fp models and quantized fallbacks
Preferred GPU types for Dedicated: H100 preferred for peak bursts, A100 acceptable for steady state; support for mixed instance pool
Data handling: VPC-only control plane, customer-managed KMS, audit logs retained 13 months, EU residency for EU customers
sizing_baseline: Initial sizing recommends 6x H100 for peak headroom (900 QPS bursts + rerank windows) with autoscale to 10x H100 for extreme peaks; a steady state of 3x A100-sized nodes for baseline throughput and batching efficiency.
performance_targets: Throughput guarantee: baseline 180 QPS sustained, burst capacity to 900 QPS with <5s warm-up
Latency SLOs: p95 chat <=150ms, p99 <=350ms (negotiable), rerank p95 <=350ms
Availability SLA: 99.9% monthly for Dedicated pool; runbook and fallback model routing included
poc_plan: POC duration: 72h stress/perf window after workshop
POC objectives: validate p95 latency at target QPS, verify KV cache hit rates and batching efficiency, measure token/sec cost delta between quantized and fp32 variants
Instrumentation: Redwood Console dashboards + request-level tracing; customer to provide synthetic workload generator and historical traffic trace
Success criteria: maintain p95 targets for 3/4 of test windows and demonstrate predictable cost curve under burst scenarios
negotiation_notes: Customer insists on contractual clause for model fallback behavior and cost-per-token ceilings during declared peak events
Procurement wants 12-month committed plan with quarterly review; asks for sample SLA language referencing p95 and mitigation credits
